name: Flexus700
lines: - Dual Vortex Groove + Solid Foaming เพิ่มร่องพิเศษบริเวณด้านในของเฟรมส่วนบนและล่าง ช่วยเพิ่มความยืดหยุ่นของเฟรม ขณะสัมผัสลูก ทำให้สามารถ Hold ลูกได้ดียิ่งขึ้น ให้ฟิลสัมผัสที่นุ่มนวล พร้อมช่วยควบคุมทิศทางและเพิ่มความแม่นยำในการคอลโทรล
- 6.6 Super Elastic Shaft ก้านขนาด 6.6 mm. เวอร์ชั่นใหม่ สปริงตัวได้ดีขึ้น พร้อมการควบคุมที่แม่นยำ
- 30T Mitsubishi Carbon Sheet โครงสร้างคาร์บอนเกรดพรีเมียมทั้งชิ้น เสริมความแข็งแกร่งให้ตัวไม้ เพิ่มความนิ่งของเฟรม และความแม่นยำในทุกช็อต พร้อมรองรับเกมบุกที่รวดเร็วและรุนแรง

ทำให้มีความแข็งแรงและความยืดหยุ่นสูง
โครงสร้างโฟมเจเนอเรชันใหม่ พัฒนาต่อยอดจาก MuCell Foam ด้วยโครงสร้างภายในที่หนาแน่นและไร้รอยต่อ ช่วยเพิ่มความแข็งแรง ลดการสูญเสียพลังงาน พร้อมมอบเสถียรภาพและสัมผัสการตีที่แน่น มั่นคงยิ่งขึ้น

name: Yonex Voltric Lite (Black/Yellow) (Pre-Strung)
lines: VOLTRIC LITE combines incredible power and fast racket handling for the first time, making this the perfect racket for players seeking exceptional ‘all-round’ performance.

Traditionally, extra weight at the top of the racquet frame has increased hitting power but reduced the speed of racquet handling. In contrast, a lighter top to the frame increases speed but causes a loss of hitting power.

For the first time, the new TRI-VOLTAGE SYSTEM successfully combines the contrasting characteristics of exceptional power and great handling. YONEX has developed a racquet which achieves the combination of heavy smashes and speedy racquet handling.

: The stiff racquet structure at the top of the frame allows the head to bend in a very controlled way and hold shuttles on the string bed for longer. The thin frame sides then allow the frame to flex more and transfer more energy to the shuttle. This combination allows you to smash with instant power.

: In VOLTRIC, the weight is balanced on the top of the frame and at the joint area which allows good handling while also maintaining power. The thin sides of the frame and at the top of the head reduce air resistance and improve the handling even further. Players can now make a full swing even during short range rallies as VOLTRIC responds instantly to even subtle movements.
The square-shaped ISOMETRIC frame shape is designed to keep vertical strings at a similar length, as well as the horizontal strings to produce an expanded sweet spot in all directions.
Combines solid hitting feel and quick swing.

It works by acting as an adhesive, bonding the graphite fiber with the resin to create a stronger and more flexible frame. Additionally, the material helps the racket return to its original state quickly after making contact with the shuttlecock, allowing for a more rapid follow-up shot.

The Isometric frame shape is square-shaped, designed to keep vertical and horizontal strings at similar lengths to produce a larger sweet spot in all directions. The Aero+Box Frame provides a solid hitting feel and quick swing, improving overall racket performance.

The new Built-in T-Joint is made of lightweight plastic combined with epoxy resin and a foaming agent to enhance stability and performance by improving shuttle control on the string bed and in the air. Finally, the Control Support Cap provides an 88% wider flat surface compared to a regular racket, allowing for better grip, faster follow-through, and sharper maneuverability.

We recommend Li-Ning AXForce 100 II for advanced and technically strong badminton players looking for a high-end racket for attacking play and who have the technique needed to control its performance.

name: Yonex ArcSaber 11 Tour - Demo Rental
lines: The Yonex ArcSaber 11 Tour badminton racquet delivers decisive control  and more reach thanks to a stable frame construction and increased shuttle contact time on the string bed. The Yonex ArcSaber 11 Tour is a true all-round badminton racquet that is 10 mm longer than conventional length frames giving you more leverage on smashes and better reach on digs. This makes the Yonex ArcSaber 11 Tour a powerhouse on offense and defense. This racquet delivers great frame stability thanks to its new frame structure that has a stiff upper and bottom of the racquet face to reduce twisting at impact. Adding to the Yonex ArcSaber 11's stability is Yonex's Control-Assist Bumper, a grommet piece at 12 o'clock on the frame featuring T-Anchor, that help lock in vertical strings for more consistent movement, improving accuracy. The Yonex ArcSaber 11 extends shuttle contact time, the side of this racquet has a softer feel thanks to its construction, promoting more flexibility around the sweet spot. Pocketing Booster, a proprietary rubber-like material strategically lines a portion of the frame increasing the elasticity of the frame' flex and positively impact shuttle hold and launch speed. Players that want some added reach on both offense and defense can rely on the Yonex ArcSaber 11 Tour to deliver control, power and an all-around great performance.
Yonex ArcSaber 11 Tour Badminton Racquet Specs:
Composition: H.M. Graphite, Super HMG, Ultra PE Fiber

The Yonex ArcSaber 7 Pro provides players with great frame stability thanks to its new frame structure that has a stiff upper and bottom of the racquet face to reduce twisting at impact. The Yonex ArcSaber 7 Pro extends shuttle contact time, the side of this racquet has a softer feel thanks to its construction, promoting more flexibility around the sweet spot. Pocketing Booster, a proprietary rubber-like material strategically lines a portion of the frame increasing the elasticity of the frame' flex and positively impact shuttle hold and launch speed. The Yonex ArcSaber 7 Pro is a great all-around badminton racquet that has a medium flex and maneuverable thanks to its even balance while providing improved dwell time on your shots.

name: Yonex ASTROX 99 Tour (Cherry Sunburst, Factory Strung)
lines: The Yonex ASTROX 99 Tour badminton racquet brings more power to a wider range of players. The Yonex ASTROX 99 Tour features wider grommets and a modified isometric head shape to deliver more power and longer contact with the shuttle. The stiff flex of the Yonex Astrox 99's shaft gives intermediate and advanced players a reliable racquet that you can swing hard and with confidence. With a head heavy balance, players can put more power and speed on their shots to keep opponents guessing. Yonex has made this offensive style racquet more versatile with Wide Diameter Grommets and a modified Isometric head shape. Wide Diameter Grommets are larger grommets are strategically placed at 3 and 9 o'clock on the racquet head for more string movement and shuttle contact time. The modified Isometric head shape is wider in the 4 corners and strategically reinforced for stronger contact and creates a larger and more forgiving sweet spot. Designed for a wide range of players, the Yonex ASTROX 99 Tour is an offensive powerhouse with a stiff flex to suit intermediate and advanced players.
Yonex ASTROX 99 Tour Badminton Racquet (Cherry Sunburst) Specs:

name: Yonex ASTROX 99 Pro (White Tiger)
lines: The Yonex ASTROX 99 Pro badminton racquet is a powerhouse designed for offensive and attacking players and is the racquet of choice for Kento Mamota. The Yonex ASTROX 99 Pro features an updated bumper, wider grommets and a modified isometric head shape to give you an edge. The Power-Assist Bumper is a tungsten infused weighted bumper that delivers more raw power. Heavier than conventional grommets, Power-Assist Bumper adds 55% more weight than conventional grommets to make smashes and attacking shots more devastating to your opponents by transferring more weight and speed into the shuttle. To make the overall racquet more forgiving and adaptable on defense, Yonex has included Wide Diameter Grommets and a modified Isometric head shape. Wide Diameter Grommets are larger grommets are strategically placed at 3 and 9 o'clock on the racquet head for more string movement and shuttle contact time. The modified Isometric head shape is wider in the 4 corners and strategically reinforced for stronger contact and creates a larger and more forgiving sweet spot. Players that can smash hand handle the head heavy balance with stiff flex will be able to take advantage of the updated tech in the Yonex ASTROX 99 Pro making this another great option for offensive and attacking badminton players.
Yonex ASTROX 99 Pro Badminton Racquet (White Tiger) Specs:

lines: – The popular ASTROX 99 series known for generating dominating smash power, is coming out with new technology and a new look ― in collaboration with men’s singles World No1. Kento Momota. The new ASTROX 99 will be available in late-September with a design reveal on September 1st.

Like the ASTROX 88 S/D models, the new ASTROX 99 will be available to a wider audience with versions PRO, TOUR, GAME, and PLAY, designed and crafted with the same performance concept for different levels of play.

The ASTROX 99 is a head-heavy power racquet, boasting the heaviest swing weight of the ASTROX series. It’s known to generate a single, powerful smash, often too heavy to be speedy in recovery. In response, Yonex worked hand in hand with Kento Momota to craft a racquet that would give him both power and the ability to convert defensive plays into offense; the result is an improved ASTROX 99 where decisive power is accompanied by extended shuttle hold for enhanced defensive shot-making.

The new ASTROX 99* is equipped with the POWER-ASSIST BUMPER, a tungsten-infused weighted bumper installed at the top of the frame transferring additional weight to the shuttle for more powerful smashes. To enhance defensive shot-making, Wide Diameter Grommets are strategically placed on the frame sides, allowing strings to shift at impact for emphasized shuttle pocketing. The iconic ISOMETRIC frame has been modified by strengthening frame corners to adjust the shape and expand the sweet spot.

Boosted power with a tungsten-infused weighted bumper, adding 55% more weight* than conventional grommets. The POWER-ASSIST BUMPER enhances the Rotational Generator System, quickly transferring more weight to the shuttle.

Intricate weight distribution technology designed with the counterbalance theory that allows head-heavy racquets to recover faster between shots. By employing the VOLUME CUT RESIN and POWER-ASSIST BUMPER, the new ASTROX 99 models have a further refined Rotational Generator System where intricate weight distribution can be taken to the next level.

New ASTROX 77: This Power Is Ours
TOKYO, Japan – Power is an integral characteristic of the ASTROX family. For racquets in
the ASTROX line-up, the head-heavy nature of the series means strength is pertinent to

unlocking the raw power. The brand new ASTROX 77 is different -- power is effortless and accessible to all. The new ASTROX 77 is designed with a mid-flex shaft and a maneuverable, slightly heavy head which grants extra power for a wide range of players from intermediate to advanced. This second-generation sports improvements in the hitting feel by enhancing shock absorption, and in power by balancing snapback and flex. The racquet will hit store shelves worldwide in late October.
The original ASTROX 77 is designed for intermediate to advanced players looking to

dominate the court with steep smashes. It is equipped with the Rotational Generator System that enables quick recovery for a continuous stream of powerful attacks. The racquet utilizes NamdTM throughout the shaft producing more flex and a faster snapback.  The new ASTROX 77 is a further evolved version of its predecessor, featuring new technologies for better performances and a 2.9% increase in smash power. The joint at the bottom of the frame is composed of a new resin material, Flex Fuse, which combines a shock-absorbing material with base resin for a softer feel on impact. The new elongated shaft is equipped with NamdTM, a carbon-graphite material that generates quick snapback to
accompany the extra flex. The addition of the E.B.CAP PLUS (Energy Boost Cap Plus) is used for further snapback.
The new ASTROX 77 will be seen in the hands of Tokyo Olympic Gold Medalist, Chen Yu
Fei (CHN), World Tour Finals 2021 champion, An Se Young (KOR), 2022 World

Championships mixed doubles winner, Huang Ya Qiong (CHN), and 2022 Malaysia Masters champion, Fajar Alfian (INA). The racquets are scheduled for a global launch on October 21st, 2022, in three different models, PRO, TOUR and PLAY – each developed with the same performance concept but with variations in performance materials used.

lines: is built on the 3D Calibar Technology Platform and features a high-tech, geometric badminton racket frame design that greatly reduces air resistance. It produces faster swing speeds for bigger smashes and gains outstanding reviews from strong players that are looking for maximum power.

Li-Ning DRIVE Series badminton rackets feature a stiffer shaft and highly elastic head design for rapid repulsion power. Suitable for fast players that are skilled in switching quickly between offence and defense.
The 3D Calibar Technology Platform uses a 3-digit numbering system.The first digit determines the grade of the racket as follows:
If the first digit is 1, 2 or 3, the racket is suitable for beginners.
If the first digit is 4, 5 or 6, the racket is suitable for intermediate players.
If the first digit is 7, 8 or 9, the racket is suitable for advanced players.

Strings not included. Please see Available Options above for professional stringing services performed on a cutting edge Li-Ning electronic stringing machine using your choice of best-in-class Li-Ning badminton strings.

Introducing aviation technology to control the racket frame. After impact, Li-Ning rackets absorb unnecessary shaking from vibrations and restore the racket’s outer “wings” back to a precision performance mode. This readies the player for a quick, precise and stable follow up stroke.

Li-Ning takes the extra step to avoid imperfections sometimes caused by machine processing of other rackets. By implementing multi-layer carbon fibers, the racket is crafted with strength and longevity in mind.

Li-Ning rackets are manufactured with a sweet spot that extends upward. The hitting point is moved higher, providing a larger defensive area. This considerably improves hitting velocity due to a wider stringed area and increased bounce strength.

Implementing real data compiled from the field, Li-Ning manufactures the most aerodynamic rackets possible. Advanced calculations have resulted in rackets with extremely low drag and higher intensity.
The nanometer technology combines the carbon fiber and resin more closely. This method provides better elasticity, stability and durability – resulting in more powerful striking.

We filled the slim shafts of our rackets with the same aramid fibers found in helmets. These heat-resistant and strong synthetic fibers provide world-class flexibility and durability. This is another way Li-Ning helps avoid sports injuries.

Our proprietary process thoroughly mixes resins with carbon fibers to ensure all our rackets are manufactured in a uniform manner. This provides optimum strength and consistent performance no matter which racket you choose.
These slim-grooved grommets lock in and protect the exposed portion of the string along the edges of the racket. They help provide shock absorption to make your shots even more accurate.

With a Stabilized Torsion Angle, shots that are not hit with the sweet spot of the racket are designed to act almost as if they were. This torsion resistance performance allows the frame to remain stabilized for an even hitting surface.
By changing the shaft’s recoil point, our rackets quickly bend and rebound back into position, so you are ready for the continuous volley and attack.

Four Types of Aeronaut Badminton Control Playing Styles

Li-Ning realizes that players want to be in control of their shots, but that all shots are not created equal. If you are searching for a control type racket, in the Aeronaut Technology series, choose according to your strengths:
For fast players who can switch quickly between offense and defense these rackets feature a stiffer shaft and highly-elastic head.
For well-rounded, experienced players these rackets are built with a moderate balance point and medium shaft.
For strong, aggressive players who want to maximize their power, these rackets are designed with a heavier head and higher balance point.
For players who want to combine a lightweight racket with aggressive speed and agility, these rackets have flexible shafts and weigh less than 80 grams.

dominate the court with steep smashes. It is equipped with the Rotational Generator System that enables quick recovery for a continuous stream of powerful attacks. accompany the extra flex. The addition of the E.B.CAP PLUS (Energy Boost Cap Plus) is used for further snapback.

Fei (CHN), World Tour Finals 2021 champion, An Se Young (KOR), 2022 World

Championships mixed doubles winner, Huang Ya Qiong (CHN), and 2022 Malaysia Masters champion, Fajar Alfian (INA). name: Yonex ASTROX 99 Play Strung Badminton Racket [Cherry Sunburst]
lines: – The popular ASTROX 99 series known for generating dominating smash power, is coming out with new technology and a new look ― in collaboration with men’s singles World No1. Kento Momota. The new ASTROX 99 goes a step beyond unequivocal raw power, gaining the ability to control the pace of the game. The new ASTROX 99 will be available in late-September with a design reveal on September 1st.

Like the ASTROX 88 S/D models, the new ASTROX 99 will be available to a wider audience with versions PRO, TOUR, GAME, and PLAY, designed and crafted with the same performance concept for different levels of play.

The ASTROX 99 is a head-heavy power racquet, boasting the heaviest swing weight of the ASTROX series. It’s known to generate a single, powerful smash, often too heavy to be speedy in recovery. In response, Yonex worked hand in hand with Kento Momota to craft a racquet that would give him both power and the ability to convert defensive plays into offense; the result is an improved ASTROX 99 where decisive power is accompanied by extended shuttle hold for enhanced defensive shot-making.

The new ASTROX 99* is equipped with the POWER-ASSIST BUMPER, a tungsten-infused weighted bumper installed at the top of the frame transferring additional weight to the shuttle for more powerful smashes. To enhance defensive shot-making, Wide Diameter Grommets are strategically placed on the frame sides, allowing strings to shift at impact for emphasized shuttle pocketing. The iconic ISOMETRIC frame has been modified by strengthening frame corners to adjust the shape and expand the sweet spot.

Boosted power with a tungsten-infused weighted bumper, adding 55% more weight* than conventional grommets. The POWER-ASSIST BUMPER enhances the Rotational Generator System, quickly transferring more weight to the shuttle.

Intricate weight distribution technology designed with the counterbalance theory that allows head-heavy racquets to recover faster between shots. By employing the VOLUME CUT RESIN and POWER-ASSIST BUMPER, the new ASTROX 99 models have a further refined Rotational Generator System where intricate weight distribution can be taken to the next level.
Control the shuttle-release timing with larger grommets designed for more string movement, extending the shuttle contact time.
The iconic ISOMETRIC head shape is enhanced for a larger, more forgiving sweet spot. Frame sides are strategically reinforced with wider areas for a stronger construct.

Common technologies throughout the ASTROX 100 series.
1. Expanded Sweet Spot in Modified Frame

Compared to regular round frames, Yonex’s original ISOMETRIC frame creates a wider sweet spot. The ASTROX 100 frame has been slightly modified into an even more square-like shape, increasing the already wide sweet spot by 2.9%
, while maintaining the same overall frame size. Benefits of this evolved ISOMETRIC shape include increased power on strong and continuous shots even if they don’t hit the center of the racquet.
A new structure reduces shaft twisting and increases its flexibility. Thumb fitting shape transmits even more power to the shuttle.
Differences between the ASTROX 100 ZZ and the ASTROX 100 ZX models.

. While the use of Black Micro Core material puts more weight on the head of the frame. A new built-in T-joint, which is 1.3%

lighter than any other Yonex racquet, allows the racquet to have a lower weight distribution. By redesigning the racquet’s weight distribution in this manner, high rotational power needed for strong continuous smashes is generated.

Designed with the slimmest shaft in the history of Yonex racquets
, this ASTROX model, traditionally hollow inside, uses graphite material in the core, resulting in an 11.8%
reduction in air resistance. By making the shaft solid, resilience is increased, further allowing strong continuous shots.

Rexis is a high-performance shaft precisely designed through an advanced molding technique with High-Quality, ingenuitive, Performance Graphite material. It has surpassed Yonex’s quality standards.

By utilizing high quality Namd graphite throughout the shaft and frame of both models more flex is produced with a faster snapback, unleashing dramatic steep power. The material stays flexible even with increased swing speed, bending when swing speed increases and restoring its original hard shape at the end of the swing. The ability to bend even further and snap back rapidly, produces stronger shots and greater smash speeds.

lines: The AERONAUT 9000C badminton racket is built on the Aeronaut Technology Platform that has a unique air-stream channel integrated into the racket head. This reduces air resistance which helps to generate faster shuttlecock speeds. It’s suitable for players looking for the best control with little to no sacrifice in power.
Li-Ning COMBAT rackets have a heavier head and a higher balance point. Suitable for very strong, aggressive players looking for MAXIMUM power.
The AERONAUT Technology Platform uses a 4-digit numbering system. The first digit determines the grade of the racket as follows:
If the first digit is 1, 2 or 3, the racket is suitable for beginners.
If the first digit is 4, 5 or 6, the racket is suitable for intermediate players.
If the first digit is 7, 8 or 9, the racket is suitable for advanced players.
TENSION: Vertical < 32 lbs lbs, Horizontal < 32 lbs

Introducing aviation technology to control the racket frame. After impact, Li-Ning rackets absorb unnecessary shaking from vibrations and restore the racket’s outer “wings” back to a precision performance mode. This readies the player for a quick, precise and stable follow up stroke.

Li-Ning takes the extra step to avoid imperfections sometimes caused by machine processing of other rackets. By implementing multi-layer carbon fibers, the racket is crafted with strength and longevity in mind.

DLi-Ning rackets are manufactured with a sweet spot that extends upward. The hitting point is moved higher, providing a larger defensive area. This considerably improves hitting velocity due to a wider stringed area and increased bounce strength.

Implementing real data compiled from the field, Li-Ning manufactures the most aerodynamic rackets possible. Advanced calculations have resulted in rackets with extremely low drag and higher intensity.
The nanometer technology combines the carbon fiber and resin more closely. This method provides better elasticity, stability and durability – resulting in more powerful striking.

We filled the slim shafts of our rackets with the same aramid fibers found in helmets. These heat-resistant and strong synthetic fibers provide world-class flexibility and durability. This is another way Li-Ning helps avoid sports injuries.

Our proprietary process thoroughly mixes resins with carbon fibers to ensure all our rackets are manufactured in a uniform manner. This provides optimum strength and consistent performance no matter which racket you choose.
These slim-grooved grommets lock in and protect the exposed portion of the string along the edges of the racket. They help provide shock absorption to make your shots even more accurate.

With a Stabilized Torsion Angle, shots that are not hit with the sweet spot of the racket are designed to act almost as if they were. This torsion resistance performance allows the frame to remain stabilized for an even hitting surface.

lines: The Yonex Astrox 100 badminton racquet is targeted at advanced players and designed to deliver power from hit after hit. The innovative Rotational Generator System, introduced through the ASTROX series earlier, has been further enhanced for the ASTROX 100. More precise weight distribution throughout the grip end, frame top and the joint increases the rotational power. These enhancements ensure the momentum for quicker consecutive shots. Namd, which produces more flex and a faster snap-back, is used throughout the frame and shaft, unleashing dramatic steep power. The synergy created from the Rotational Generator System enables continuous powerful attacks. Similar to the ASTROX 99, the ASTROX 100 ZZ (AX100ZZ) has utilized next-generation graphite Namd in the entire body, which results in a large increase in the snap-back speed of the shaft, producing greater smash speeds and doubling contact time with the shuttle, resulting in an explosive shot as the racquet returns from flexed to straight at the end of the swing. Additionally, the Energy Boost Cap shape is designed to encourage even more flex in the shaft, further benefiting from the effects of the Namd graphite. The series trademark technology, Rotational Generator System, which contributes to a smooth transition from shot to shot also helps the player maximize the effects of the entire Namd body. In high-performance racquets, it is common to combine nanomaterials with resin that connects graphite fibers, but in Namd, nanomaterials adhere directly to the graphite fibers and the degree of adhesion between graphite fibers and resin is greatly increased. This major improvement produces a shaft that flexes and stores energy, delivering explosive force on impact with the shuttle. From the initial movement of the player to the impact, the new dimension graphite is difficult to harden, and the shaft extends and accumulates energy due to the speed of the fast swing. Since the follow-through of the swing is smaller after direct impact with the shuttle, the swing speed drops and the new dimension graphite regains hardness and strengthens the resilience of the shaft, allowing the energy to explode rapidly before returning to its original state. By applying the counterbalance theory, weight is distributed throughout the grip end, frame top and the joint for maximum control. The transition to the next shot can be performed smoothly with rapid succession.

lines: The Babolat Super Tape X5 is a pack of five pre-cut protective strips that shield the top of a racket frame — the grommets and head guard — from the scuffing that comes with court contact and mishits. A few seconds to apply, and it adds months to the life of the parts that wear out first.

— peel, position along the head, press down.

The head guard is the first thing to go on any racket that gets used properly — a scraped serve, a low volley, a frame that clips the court on a stretch. Once the grommet strip wears through, the string starts running on bare graphite and breakages follow. Super Tape sits over that zone and takes the damage instead, and when it is worn you peel it off and fit the next strip.

Five strips cost a fraction of a grommet replacement and far less than a restring cycle cut short by frame wear. For anyone who plays on abrasive surfaces or who scrapes the frame regularly, this is the cheapest protection available for an expensive racket.

name: Victor Thruster HMR Pro Badminton Racket (Gold)
lines: God of Sports Expert Verdict on Victor Thruster HMR Pro Badminton Racket (Gold):

The Victor Thruster HMR Pro Badminton Racket is Victor's updated take on its classic Thruster Hammer, the attacking frame that made "HMR" one of the best-known names in club badminton. It keeps the Hammer's head-heavy balance and flexible shaft, and builds them into a stronger, box-shaped frame reinforced with Victor's Fiber Reinforced System (FRS).

At 4U (about 80 to 84 grams) with a G5 grip, it has a full, solid swingweight. The weight sits towards the head, so clears and smashes carry real momentum, while the flexible 6.8mm shaft loads up on the backswing and releases that energy into the shuttle. Smashing feels easy and natural, even before your technique and wrist speed are fully developed.

The reinforced frame is what makes this the "Pro" version. It is rated up to 32 lbs, which is unusually high for a flexible, intermediate frame, and the box-shaped section stays stable on off-centre hits instead of twisting. That gives developing players room to raise tension as their game sharpens, without changing racket.

This is a step up for intermediate players who want proper Victor attacking quality without jumping to advanced-tier pricing. Players who already have a fast, compact swing, or who play mainly at the front of the court, will get more from a stiffer or lighter frame.
Technology Breakdown of the Victor Thruster HMR Pro Badminton Racket:
Head-heavy balance — momentum into every attack:
Extra weight towards the head keeps the racket travelling through the shuttle on clears and smashes, so you get depth and pace without forcing the swing.
The shaft bends on the backswing and kicks back at contact, adding pace for players whose swing speed is still building. The slim 6.8mm profile also cuts through the air with less drag.
Box-shaped frame — stability and higher tension:
A squarer frame section resists twisting on off-centre contact and holds string tension well, which is why the frame is rated up to 32 lbs.
Fiber Reinforced System (FRS) — a stronger frame:
Layers of reinforcing fibre in the graphite and resin frame add strength and keep the frame feeling solid and controlled when strung tight.
Performance Ratings of the Victor Thruster HMR Pro Badminton Racket:
Head-heavy balance and a flexible shaft make steep, heavy smashes easy to produce, even with a developing swing.
The flexible shaft helps lift and block with little effort; the head weight needs a moment more to reset against fast smashes.
The stable box frame gives a clean, predictable response on net shots and tight lifts.
A stable frame and the option to string up to 32 lbs give good placement control for an attacking racket.
On Court Performance Analysis of the Victor Thruster HMR Pro Badminton Racket:

Clears are where the flexible shaft and head weight work best together. The shaft does much of the work, so full-length clears come with relatively little effort, and the racket stays comfortable late in long rallies when your arm starts to tire.

This is the racket's main strength. The head weight carries momentum into the shuttle and the flexible shaft adds a whip at contact, giving steep, heavy smashes that feel easy to produce. Players still building wrist speed will notice the extra pace straight away.
Flat drives are solid and stable thanks to the box frame, but the head-heavy balance makes the racket a touch slower to bring back in very fast, repeated exchanges. Shorter, compact swings help here.

Defence is better than most attacking frames at this level. The flexible shaft helps lift and block the shuttle back deep with little effort, though the head weight asks for early preparation against hard, fast smashes.
Net play is reliable and predictable. The stable frame gives a clean response on dribbles and tight net lifts, and stringing a little higher sharpens touch further as your control improves.

Handling is steady rather than fast. At 4U with the weight towards the head, it is built for power first; players who want lightning-quick reactions at the front of the court will find a lighter or even-balanced racket quicker.
Racket Finder — Is the Victor Thruster HMR Pro Badminton Racket Right for You?
Intermediate players building an attacking game:
the head-heavy balance and flexible shaft make smashing easy and natural while technique is still developing.
Players stepping up from a beginner racket:
a proper Victor attacking frame with room to raise string tension up to 32 lbs as your game improves.
real Victor attacking quality without moving to advanced-tier pricing.

a stiffer frame will give you more precision and control at high swing speeds.
Not for you if you play mostly at the net in doubles:
a lighter or even-balanced racket will react faster in quick front-court exchanges.
Playing Style Guide for the Victor Thruster HMR Pro Badminton Racket:
The ideal fit. The racket is built to make smashes and clears from the back of the court easy and powerful.
Workable, with a stable and predictable feel at the net, but the head weight makes it slower than a dedicated speed racket in rapid exchanges.

lines: God of Sports Expert Verdict on Maxbolt Navigator II Badminton Racket (Pink):

name: Yonex Arcsaber 1 Ability Badminton Racket (Black/Red)
lines: God of Sports Expert Verdict on Yonex Arcsaber 1 Ability Badminton Racket (Black/Red):

The Yonex Arcsaber 1 Ability Badminton Racket (Black/Red) is an entry-level all-round racket in Yonex's Arcsaber family, the line built around control and shuttle hold. It is aimed squarely at players who are new to the game or moving up from a basic aluminium or steel racket, and it gives them a light graphite Yonex frame without the demands of a competition racket.

Retail specifications agree on the core build: a graphite frame and shaft, a flexible shaft, a slightly head-heavy balance and a maximum string tension of 30 lbs. The flexible shaft is the key point for a beginner. It bends and springs back on each stroke, adding power to a swing that is still developing, so clears reach further for the same effort.

The Arcsaber 1 comes in three versions, Feel, Clear and Ability, which share the same frame and specifications and differ in design and colour. That means you can choose the look you like without giving anything up on court. This listing is the Ability in Black/Red.

It suits beginners, school and academy players, and recreational players who play a few times a week. The honest caveat is that it is not built for competitive match play. Strong club players with a fast swing will find the flexible shaft too soft for steep smashes and quick drives.
Technology Breakdown of the Yonex Arcsaber 1 Ability Badminton Racket (Black/Red):

A flexible shaft bends more during the swing and releases that energy at impact. For a newer player, that means clears and lifts travel further without forcing the stroke, and mistimed shots are more forgiving.
A graphite frame is far lighter and stiffer than aluminium or steel, so the racket is easier to swing for long sessions and the frame stays steady on contact.
Slightly head-heavy balance — a little help overhead:

Retailers place the balance point at around 290 to 295 mm. That small amount of extra weight towards the head helps carry the racket through clears and smashes, while the frame stays light enough to move quickly in defence.
The Arcsaber family is Yonex's control line. At this level, the practical result is a racket that feels predictable and easy to place, which helps a beginner build consistent strokes.
A 30 lbs limit gives plenty of room. Beginners will get the best results well below that, usually between 20 and 24 lbs (see the FAQs).

Smashes and clears are easy to get going thanks to the flexible shaft and slight head weight. It lacks the stiffness and mass for steep, heavy smashes at a higher level.
The light frame is quick to bring across the body for blocks and lifts, and the flexible shaft helps lift the shuttle high and deep. Very hard smashes can still push the soft frame around.
The strongest part of this racket in our rating. The light frame is easy to get up in front of you at the net, so pushes, net lifts and simple net kills feel natural for a newer player.
Steady and predictable for a beginner. The flexible shaft holds the shuttle a fraction longer, which helps placement, though fast exchanges expose the soft frame.
On Court Performance Analysis of the Yonex Arcsaber 1 Ability Badminton Racket (Black/Red):

Clears are where a beginner will notice the difference first. The flexible shaft adds spring to the stroke and the slight head weight carries the swing through, so the shuttle reaches the back of the court without having to force it.

Smashing is comfortable and easy to learn with, but not heavy. The flexible shaft helps a developing swing, while a strong player will find the shuttle loses steepness and speed compared with a stiffer attacking racket.
Drive rallies are manageable at recreational pace. In fast exchanges the soft shaft takes a moment to recover between shots, so a compact swing works better than a full one.
Defence is comfortable. The frame is light enough to react quickly, and the flexible shaft makes it easy to lift the shuttle high and deep under pressure.
Basic net shots, pushes and lifts are easy to control. Very fine spinning net play is better left to a more advanced racket.
Handling is light and easy for long sessions, which suits players who are still building wrist strength and stamina.

name: Li-Ning Axforce Tiger Badminton Racket (White/Lime)
lines: God of Sports Expert Verdict on Li-Ning Axforce Tiger Badminton Racket:

The Li-Ning Axforce Tiger Badminton Racket is the entry point into Li-Ning's AxForce family, the brand's attacking series, and this White/Lime colourway is available in two weights: 4U (around 80 to 84 grams) and 5U (around 75 to 79 grams). Li-Ning describes it as delivering an "axe-like" force, and the build backs that up: a head-heavy carbon-fibre frame, a flexible shaft and a sturdy 7mm shaft diameter, rated up to 30 lbs in both weights.

The head-heavy balance is what makes it feel powerful. With more mass towards the top of the frame, the racket carries momentum through the swing, so clears reach the back line and smashes land with weight even when the swing is not perfect. The flexible shaft adds to this by bending and releasing on each stroke, which helps players who have not yet developed a fast, compact swing.

The trade-off is speed in the front and mid-court. A head-heavy frame is slower to bring back into position, so fast drive exchanges, quick blocks and net reactions take more effort than with an even or head-light racket. This is where the weight choice matters: the 5U recovers noticeably faster and is easier on the arm, while the 4U carries more weight into the smash and feels steadier when blocking hard hitters.

The Li-Ning Axforce Tiger Badminton Racket suits beginners and improving club players who want to build an attacking game. Choose the 4U for singles and the heaviest possible smash; choose the 5U for doubles, long sessions and quicker handling. Players who outgrow it can step up to the AxForce 90 Tiger Max, the flagship of the same Tiger line.
Technology Breakdown of the Li-Ning Axforce Tiger Badminton Racket:
Head-heavy balance — weight behind every overhead:
More of the racket's mass sits towards the head in both weights. On court this gives the swing more momentum, so smashes feel heavier and clears travel further for the same effort.
Flexible shaft — power from a developing swing:
The shaft bends as you swing and springs back at contact, adding pace to the shuttle. This is especially helpful for newer players whose timing and wrist speed are still improving.

The 4U frame (80 to 84 grams) puts more mass through the shuttle for heavier smashes and steadier blocks. The 5U frame (75 to 79 grams) swings faster, recovers more quickly between shots and puts less load on the shoulder and elbow.
7mm shaft and carbon-fibre frame — durable and forgiving:
Li-Ning lists a 7mm shaft. Together with the carbon-fibre construction, it keeps the frame stable and robust for regular club play.
Li-Ning rates both weights up to 30 lbs, which leaves plenty of room. Most beginners will play best well below that limit (see the FAQs).
Performance Ratings of the Li-Ning Axforce Tiger Badminton Racket:

The head-heavy balance and flexible shaft are built for attack. Smashes and clears come off with real weight, even for players still developing their swing. The 4U hits slightly heavier; the 5U lets you smash repeatedly without tiring.
The heavy head makes quick blocks and flat defensive returns slower to set up. The 5U reacts faster; the 4U holds steadier against hard smashes.
Workable at the net for drops and net shots, but the head-heavy balance is slower in quick net exchanges than a head-light frame, especially in 4U.
The weight in the head keeps the frame steady on contact, so drops and clears go where they are aimed. Very fast flat exchanges are harder to control.
On Court Performance Analysis of the Li-Ning Axforce Tiger Badminton Racket:

This is one of the racket's best areas. The head-heavy balance and flexible shaft combine to send clears and high tosses to the back line with very little effort, which is exactly what a developing player needs to push opponents to the rear court. The 5U keeps that easy length late into a long session.

Smashing is the racket's main purpose. The weight in the head gives smashes a heavy feel, and the flexible shaft adds whip to the swing. The 4U produces the heavier smash; the 5U trades a little weight for a faster swing and less fatigue in repeated attacks.

Fast flat drives are the hardest part of its game. The heavier head takes longer to get back into position between shots, most noticeably in the 4U. The 5U stays with mid-court drive rallies much better, though it is still not as quick as a head-light racket.

Lifting the shuttle high and deep is easy thanks to the power in the frame. Blocking a fast smash short to the net needs good preparation because the head is slow to react. The 5U comes across the body more quickly; the 4U is less likely to be pushed back by a hard smash.
Net shots and drops are consistent, and the steady frame helps with simple net play. Fine touch and quick net kills are less natural than with a head-light racket.

Handling is the clear compromise of a head-heavy racket, and the main difference between the two weights. The 4U rewards players who like longer rallies with lifts and clears; the 5U is noticeably quicker between shots and suits attacking doubles.
Racket Finder for the Li-Ning Axforce Tiger Badminton Racket — Is This Right for You?
Beginners who want to play an attacking game:
The racket helps you generate power on clears and smashes while your technique develops.
More weight behind clears and smashes, and a steadier frame against hard shots.
Smash power with enough speed to stay with the next shot.
Players who tire over long sessions (choose 5U):
The lighter frame reduces the load on the shoulder and elbow.
Not for you if you play mainly at the net:
A head-heavy frame will feel slow at the front. An even-balance racket such as the Li-Ning Halbertec 1000 is a better fit.
Not for you if you are already an advanced attacker:
Stronger players will get more from a higher-tier AxForce frame such as the AxForce Cannon or AxForce 90 Tiger Max.
Playing Style Guide for the Li-Ning Axforce Tiger Badminton Racket:
The best fit, in either weight. Clears and smashes are where this racket shines.
A strong fit, especially in 5U, which recovers quickly enough to handle the drive or block that comes back.
A good fit at beginner and club level, especially in 4U. The power for deep clears and lifts makes it easier to move an opponent around the court.
Not ideal. The head-heavy balance makes quick net reactions and fast blocks harder; choose an even-balance or head-light racket for this role.

lines: God of Sports Expert Verdict on Li-Ning Halbertec Mage Badminton Racket (5U):

The Li-Ning Halbertec Mage Badminton Racket (5U) is the lighter version of the control model in Li-Ning's 2026 trilogy, which pairs the Mage for placement with the AxForce Warrior for power and the BladeX Assassin for speed. It keeps the even balance and the 6.8mm Modulus Slim Shaft of the 4U, but drops to the 5U weight class with a G6 grip, and Li-Ning gives it a more flexible shaft and a 29 lbs maximum tension.

Those changes add up to a racket that is faster in the hand. Less mass means the head reaches the shuttle sooner on reaction shots, and the extra flex in the shaft helps the shuttle travel without a big swing. For players who spend long sessions on court, a lighter frame also puts less load on the shoulder and elbow.

The trade-off is stability. Against a hard smash or a heavy drive, a 5U frame gives way a little more than a 4U, and the softer shaft is slightly less exact on very fast flat exchanges. Players who already generate their own pace and want the steadiest possible block will be better served by the 4U.

Who it is for: doubles players who live in the front and mid-court, intermediate players who want quicker reactions and good touch at the net, and anyone who finds a 4U tiring over a long match. It is one of the most manoeuvrable control-focused Li-Ning badminton rackets at this level.
Technology Breakdown of the Li-Ning Halbertec Mage Badminton Racket (5U):
Modulus Slim Shaft (6.8mm) — less drag, quicker recovery:

The thin shaft moves through the air with little resistance. Combined with the 5U weight, the racket gets back to the ready position very quickly between shots, which is what fast doubles exchanges demand.
Flexible shaft — easier power from a compact swing:

Li-Ning rates the 5U Mage as extra flex, softer than the 4U's medium shaft. The shaft bends and returns more on each stroke, so clears and lifts reach the back without a full swing, and the arm does less of the work.
Modulus Graphite construction — steadiness in a light frame:
High-modulus carbon fibre keeps the head from twisting on slightly off-centre contact. That matters even more on a light racket, where a twisting head would otherwise send drops and pushes off line.
Even (SW) balance — control without a heavy head:
The weight is spread evenly through the frame. In a 5U racket this keeps the head feeling light and responsive at the net while still giving enough mass behind the shuttle for accurate placement.
Sonic Boom System — clearer feedback on contact:
Li-Ning uses this frame technology to sharpen sweet-spot response. A clean hit feels crisp and solid, which helps you judge contact quality on net kills and quick interceptions.
Performance Ratings of the Li-Ning Halbertec Mage Badminton Racket (5U):
The flexible shaft makes smashes easy to produce, and the even balance keeps them accurate. A 5U frame has less mass behind the shuttle, so outright smash pace is limited.
Very quick to react to body smashes and drives, and the light head makes late blocks easier. Against the heaviest smashes it gives slightly more than a 4U.
Light, responsive and easy to move at the front of the court, with good touch on spinning net shots and fast follow-up kills.
The even balance and stable graphite frame keep placement consistent, even with the lighter weight and softer shaft.
On Court Performance Analysis of the Li-Ning Halbertec Mage Badminton Racket (5U):

The flexible shaft does a lot of the work here. Clears and high lifts reach the back line with a shorter, more relaxed swing than the 4U needs, which helps players whose overhead technique is still developing. The light frame does mean less weight behind the shuttle against strong wind or slow shuttles.

Smashes come off the strings easily thanks to the shaft's kick, and the even balance keeps them on target. Steep half smashes and body smashes are the strength. Players looking for heavy, outright winners from the rear court will find the 5U lacks the mass of a head-heavy attacking racket.

This is where the 5U shines in doubles. The light frame and slim shaft let you keep up with fast drive rallies and counter-punch quickly. The softer shaft is a touch less precise than the 4U on the very fastest flat shots, so aim for the body rather than the lines when the pace is high.

Reaction speed is the main advantage. The racket is easy to bring across the body to block a smash or drive it back flat. Against a powerful smasher, expect a little more give in the frame, so firm grip pressure at contact helps keep blocks tight to the net.
Net play is excellent. The light, evenly weighted head makes soft spinning net shots and tight net replies easy, and it moves quickly to kill a loose return.

Handling is the defining quality of the 5U. It switches between forehand and backhand quickly and feels easy to move throughout a long match, which is why it suits doubles front-court play and players who tire with a heavier racket.

Clears and high tosses reach the back line comfortably once your swing is complete, because the medium-flex shaft stores and returns energy on a full stroke. Players who still clear with mostly arm and little body rotation will need to work harder than with a flexible shaft. The trade-off is that length is easy to judge, so tosses rarely sail long.

Smashes come down steep and on target rather than explosively fast. The even balance lets you hit the half smash and body smash accurately, which is how the Mage wins attacking points. Players who rely on outright speed from the rear court will find a head-heavy racket gives them more.

The 6.8mm shaft and even balance make the Mage quick in drive rallies. The racket comes back to the ready position quickly, and the stable frame keeps flat pushes low over the tape instead of floating up into the opponent's hitting zone.

Defence is one of the strongest parts of this racket. Blocks to the net and lifts to the back are easy to control off a fast smash, and the head does not feel heavy when you have to react late to a body shot.

Touch at the net is precise. The evenly weighted head lets you play soft spinning net shots and then switch to a quick kill if the reply is loose, and the crisp feel from the Sonic Boom System tells you immediately whether the contact was clean.

For a 4U even-balance frame, handling is quick without feeling light. The racket is easy to move between forehand and backhand at mid-court, which suits doubles front-and-back rotations as well as singles rallies.

lines: God of Sports Expert Verdict on Maxbolt Gallant Force Badminton Racket (4U):

The Maxbolt Gallant Force Badminton Racket (4U) is the attacking all-rounder of Maxbolt's Gallant series. Retailer specifications agree on the core build: a head-heavy 4U frame of around 83 to 84 grams, a medium-flex shaft, high-modulus graphite construction and a maximum string tension of 32 lbs. It sits between the stiff, high-tension Gallant Tour and the lighter-feeling Gallant Speed Slim.

The head-heavy balance gives it its attacking character. With more mass towards the top of the frame, smashes carry weight and clears reach the back line without a forced swing. The medium-flex shaft is the key difference from the Gallant Tour: it bends a little more on each stroke and adds some help to the swing, so the racket is more forgiving when your timing is not perfect.

The trade-off of any head-heavy frame applies here too. Fast drive exchanges, quick blocks and reactions at the net take more effort than with an even or head-light racket, so players who mostly play at the front of the court in doubles will feel it.

The Maxbolt Gallant Force Badminton Racket suits intermediate and competitive club players who build their game around the smash and want Gallant series power without the demands of a stiff, high-tension frame. It is a sensible step up for attacking players moving towards a more serious racket.
Technology Breakdown of the Maxbolt Gallant Force Badminton Racket (4U):
Head-heavy balance — weight behind the smash:
Retailers place the balance point at around 295 to 300mm. That extra mass towards the head adds momentum to overhead shots, making smashes heavier and clears deeper for the same effort.
Medium-flex shaft — power with some forgiveness:

A medium shaft bends and releases more than a stiff one, so it helps with power when your swing is not perfectly timed, while still keeping the shuttle on line. This is what makes it easier to use than the stiff Gallant Tour.
High-modulus graphite frame and shaft — stable on contact:
High-modulus graphite keeps the frame rigid at impact, so the energy of the swing goes into the shuttle and smashes stay accurate.
Compact frame — a concentrated hitting zone:
Retailers describe a compact frame designed for strong smashes. A compact head concentrates the frame's stiffness around the sweet spot for a solid, punchy response.
A 32 lbs limit gives plenty of room. Most intermediate players will get the best results well below that (see the FAQs).

lines: God of Sports Expert Verdict on Maxbolt Superstar 11 Badminton Racket (Red):

The Superstar 11 is the top 4U racket in Maxbolt's Superstar series and an all-rounder by design: Maxbolt pairs an even 295 mm balance with a stiff shaft, so the racket is equally at home attacking, defending and playing at the net, with a little extra punch on smashes from the stiff shaft.

Its most unusual specification is the string tension ceiling. Maxbolt rates the Superstar 11 to 43 lbs, far above the 28 to 32 lbs most rackets at this level allow, which reflects a strong 40T carbon graphite box frame. Very few players need anywhere near that tension, but it shows how robustly the frame is built.

At around 83 g (4U) with an isometric head, it is light enough to handle quickly in drives and defence, and the even balance keeps it stable on blocks. The stiff shaft gives a crisp, direct response, which buyers describe as firm and accurate, with good control over placement.

It suits intermediate players moving towards advanced play, and club players who want one racket for every part of the rally. The trade-offs are honest ones: the stiff shaft rewards a reasonably developed swing, and an even balance will not put as much weight behind a smash as a dedicated head-heavy power frame.
Even Balance (295 mm) — equally good in attack and defence:
Weight is spread evenly between head and handle, so the racket moves quickly for blocks and drives while still carrying enough head weight for solid smashes. It is the defining all-round setup.
Stiff Shaft — crisp control and attacking punch:

A stiff shaft bends less at contact, so the shuttle leaves the strings sooner and more directly. That gives precise placement and a little extra pace on smashes for a player with a reasonably fast swing.
40T Carbon Graphite Box Frame — strength and stability:
A box-shaped frame cross-section resists twisting on off-centre hits, and the strong carbon frame is what allows the very high tension rating.
Isometric Head — a forgiving sweet spot:
The squarer head shape widens the area of the string bed that gives a clean response, which helps when contact is slightly off-centre.
43 lbs Maximum Tension — a frame built to last:
One of the highest ratings at this price. It gives advanced players headroom, but most players will get the best feel well below it.
Sharp, steep smashes and fast drives come from the stiff shaft and stable frame; it hits with real punch for an even-balanced racket.
The even balance and 4U weight make blocks, lifts and counter-drives quick and stable, one of the racket's biggest strengths.
Quick and precise at the net for kills and pushes; a light, head-light speed frame is a touch faster in the very quickest exchanges.
The stiff shaft, box frame and isometric head combine for consistent, accurate placement across every shot.

a racket that does everything well, with a stiff shaft to grow into as your swing develops.
Club players who want one racket for singles and doubles:
the even balance covers attack, defence and net play without a weak area.

the stiff shaft and box frame give precise feedback on every shot.
Not for you if you want maximum smash power:
a head-heavy frame such as the Maxbolt Superstar Swift or the Yonex Astrox 100 Game VA puts more weight behind the shuttle.

a stiff shaft can feel harsh and hard to load; the medium-flex Superstar Nova or a flexible racket is easier to learn with.

a head-light 4U or a 5U frame will be quicker at the net.
The Superstar 11's natural home: steady in defence, precise in rallies and sharp enough to attack when the opening comes.
Equally comfortable at the front or the back: quick for drives and blocks, with enough punch for repeated smashes.

name: Hundred Nuclear 78 Badminton Racket (White/Red)
lines: God of Sports Expert Verdict on Hundred Nuclear 78 Badminton Racket (White/Red):

The Nuclear 78 is the heaviest racket in Hundred's lightweight Nuclear series, at 78 g. That puts it in the 5U class: a few grams lighter than the 4U frames most club players use, but far closer to them than the 72 g Nuclear 72 or the 60 g Nuclear 60.

Hundred gives it a head-heavy 305 mm balance and a Flexible 7.0 mm shaft on its Curve² frame. The head weight keeps smashes and clears feeling familiar to anyone used to a conventional attacking racket, while the lighter frame and flexible shaft make each swing easier and quicker.

That makes it the gentlest step down in weight within the series. Buyers on Hundred's site describe it as very light and easy to use, with good results on smashes, defence and net kills, and good value for money, though there are only a handful of reviews so far.

It suits beginners and improving players who want a light, forgiving racket that still attacks, and players moving down from a heavier head-heavy frame. Hundred itself rates the Nuclear series for attacking play; players who want maximum power will still get more from a 4U or 3U, and those who want the fastest possible handling should look at the lighter Nuclear models.
78 g (5U) Frame — lighter, without feeling unfamiliar:
A few grams lighter than a typical 4U, the Nuclear 78 takes less effort to swing and recover, while keeping enough mass to give smashes and clears a solid feel.
Head-Heavy Balance (305 mm) — familiar attacking feel:
More weight towards the head adds momentum to overhead shots. It is the least extreme balance in the Nuclear series, so it feels close to a conventional head-heavy racket.
The flexible shaft bends and releases at contact, which helps beginners and improving players generate pace without a fast, explosive swing.
Carbon Fibre Frame with Curve² shape — light and quick through the air:
Hundred's carbon frame keeps the weight down, and the Curve² head shape reduces air resistance for quicker swings.
Good smash power and clear depth for a 5U frame, helped by the head-heavy balance and flexible kick; a heavier 4U or 3U still hits harder.
Lighter than a 4U, so reactions are quicker, but the head-heavy balance means very fast blocks and body defence are slower than on a head-light frame.
Quick enough for interceptions and net kills; the head weight helps finish downward.
The racket's strongest area: the flexible shaft is forgiving on mistimed shots, and the light frame makes placement easy for developing players.
Racket Finder — Is This Right for You?
Players used to a regular head-heavy racket who want something lighter:
the Nuclear 78 keeps the familiar attacking feel while being easier on the arm.
the flexible shaft and light frame make power and control easier while technique develops.
Players who tire with a 4U over a long session:
a few grams less, combined with the flexible shaft, reduces the effort of every swing.
Not for you if you want the lightest, fastest racket:
the 72 g Nuclear 72 or 60 g Nuclear 60 handle faster still.
Not for you if you want maximum smash power:
a heavier head-heavy frame such as the Battle 600 at 4U puts more weight behind the shuttle.
Not for you if you are a defence-first player:
an even-balanced or head-light racket reacts faster to hard smashes.
Smashes and clears feel familiar and come easily, thanks to the head-heavy balance and flexible kick; power-first players will still find more in a 4U.
A good all-round doubles option for club play: light enough for drives and net interceptions, with enough head weight to attack when the shuttle is lifted.

Capable at the net, though dedicated net specialists will find the lighter Nuclear models quicker.

name: Hundred Nuclear 72 Badminton Racket (Orange/Black/Blue)
lines: God of Sports Expert Verdict on Hundred Nuclear 72 Badminton Racket (Orange/Black/Blue):

The Nuclear 72 sits in Hundred's lightweight Nuclear series at 72 g, a 6U frame that is noticeably lighter than the 4U rackets most club players use. It is built to make every swing easier and faster, while keeping enough weight for proper attacking shots.

Hundred pairs that light frame with a head-heavy 310 mm balance and a Flexible 7.0 mm VaporShaft. The balance puts mass where it helps smashes and clears; the flexible shaft adds kick on short, quick swings, so power comes from wrist action rather than a big backswing.

Compared with the 60 g Nuclear 60, the Nuclear 72 carries 12 g more and a less extreme balance, which gives it more solidity on smashes and blocks while staying far quicker than a 4U. Buyers on Hundred's site highlight its light weight, speed and control, and one noted the factory grip is worth replacing.

It suits intermediate players and quick-handed attackers who want faster transitions than a 4U allows, without dropping to an ultra-light frame that gives up power. Hundred rates it for advanced attacking players; it rewards good technique, and heavy-hitting rear-court players will still find more power in a 4U or 3U frame.
72 g Lightweight Frame — speed with substance:
Light enough to give quicker reactions and transitions than a 4U racket, and heavy enough to carry real weight into smashes and clears.
Hyperlight Carbon Fibre — strength at low weight:
Hundred's lightweight carbon keeps the frame rigid enough for attacking shots while holding the total weight at 72 g.
AeroBlade Frame on a Curve² shape — less air drag:
The frame is shaped to reduce air resistance, so the racket accelerates faster through the swing and recovers sooner for the next shot.
VaporShaft, Flexible 7.0 mm — power from short swings:
The flexible shaft bends and releases at contact, adding pace to quick wrist-driven drives, smashes and lifts without needing a long backswing.
Weight towards the head adds momentum to smashes and helps clears reach the back line, while the light total weight keeps handling quick.
Competitive smash power and clear depth for a 72 g frame, thanks to the head-heavy balance and flexible kick, though a 4U or 3U power racket still hits harder.
Quick to react to smashes and body shots; against very heavy hitters, the lighter frame has less mass to absorb the shuttle than a 4U.
One of the racket's strengths: the light frame gets to interceptions early, and the head weight helps push net kills down.
Easy to place drives and pushes, with buyers singling out its directional control; the flexible shaft forgives short, rushed strokes.

the Nuclear 72 gives faster handling and court coverage while keeping proper attacking power.

name: Hundred T-Fusion 500 ZOOM Badminton Racket (Red/Black)
lines: God of Sports Expert Verdict on Hundred T-Fusion 500 ZOOM Badminton Racket:

Hundred T-Fusion 500 ZOOM Badminton Racket is the most counterintuitive racket in the T-Fusion 500 triplet — and understanding why it is designed this way reveals the clarity of Hundred's engineering logic for this series. The Zoom is the lightest of the three at 79g, which would normally suggest a more neutral or speed-oriented design. But its balance point — 305mm — is the MOST head-heavy in the triplet, more extreme than the ATTK's 300mm and significantly more extreme than the CTRL's 295mm. How does the lightest frame have the most extreme head-heavy balance? Through Muscle Wingtron: strategic mass concentration at the frame crown that loads the head without adding overall weight. The result is a racket that reaches high swing velocity quickly (light total mass) while maximising the rotational momentum available at contact (305mm extreme head balance).

In playing terms, the Zoom produces a distinctly different attacking feel from the ATTK. The ATTK's 84g weight generates heavy, sustained smash pressure — the kind of rear-court singles attack that wins points through depth and pace from the baseline. The Zoom's 79g weight reaches the contact point faster, and its 305mm balance delivers a sharp, punchy momentum at impact. Fast rallies, doubles exchanges, and situations where quick preparation time is essential favour the Zoom's lighter frame. The Zoom smashes are sharp and fast rather than heavy and deep — a different offensive vocabulary suited to doubles front-foot attacking.

The Muscle Wingtron is the technology that makes this counterintuitive specification possible. By concentrating mass strategically at the crown, Hundred achieves a 305mm balance without loading the entire frame. This also reinforces the frame structure at the crown — the most stressed location during smash impact — which contributes to string tension retention and frame stability on aggressive attacks.

Curve² geometry is an especially well-considered addition on the Zoom. Because the Zoom is deployed in fast exchanges where contact precision is naturally more variable, the enlarged sweet spot means more of those fast-paced contacts produce consistent shuttle response, reducing errors in rapid doubles rallies.
Technology Breakdown of Hundred T-Fusion 500 ZOOM Badminton Racket:

Same Japan graphite as the ATTK and CTRL — tighter fibre tolerances, more consistent flex behaviour, better stiffness-to-weight ratio. At 79g, the Japan graphite helps maintain frame integrity and consistent energy transmission at the lighter overall weight — the same quality material in a lighter package than the ATTK.

Same T-Fuse construction across all three 500 variants — the monolithic shaft-frame junction that maximises elastic energy transfer. On the Zoom's lighter frame, T-Fuse ensures the energy from the flexible shaft reaches the shuttle efficiently without being dissipated at the joint.
Muscle Wingtron — Strategic Crown Mass Concentration:

The technology unique to the Zoom in this triplet. Located on the top portion of the frame, Muscle Wingtron adds strategic weight at the frame crown to maximise the balance point without adding overall frame mass. This creates the counterintuitive specification: lightest frame (79g) with most extreme head-heavy balance (305mm). Also reinforces the crown structure for string tension retention and frame stability on hard impacts.

lines: God of Sports Expert Verdict on Hundred Flareon Typhoon Badminton Racket:

The Hundred Flareon Typhoon Badminton Racket is the most distinctive racket in this group of 13 — it is the ONLY head-light balanced racket among them. Every other racket in this set (Predator 82/79, Nitrix 10, Hyfonic 1/Lazer, Flareon 100, Battle 600/900, T-Fusion 300/500 ATTK/CTRL/Zoom) is either head-heavy or even/speed-focused. The Typhoon's head-light balance places it in a fundamentally different playing category — the speed and defence specialist — making it the Hundred equivalent of a Nanoflare 700 or Auraspeed rather than an Astrox or Arcsaber.

Head-light balance is the defining technological choice that makes the Typhoon different. The centre of mass sits toward the handle rather than the frame head — producing the fastest possible wrist snap and quickest wrist recovery between shots in the entire Hundred range at GOS. This makes the Typhoon the racket of choice for: players who defend first and counter-attack second; doubles front-court specialists who need instant interceptions; drive battle specialists who need the fastest possible wrist transitions; and players whose primary playing strength is speed and reaction rather than power depth.

Torsion Stop and CNTRL Foam are the construction technologies that make the Typhoon's speed play credible at the intermediate-advanced level. In rapid exchanges where the Typhoon's speed identity is most expressed — fast drives, net rushes, counter-attacks — off-centre contact is more frequent than in measured baseline play. Torsion Stop keeps the frame face square at high-speed off-centre impact, maintaining shot direction accuracy. CNTRL Foam absorbs the accumulated vibration of many rapid-succession shots, keeping the feel clean across extended fast-rally sessions.

An honest note on the power limitation: the Typhoon's head-light balance produces lighter smash impact than head-heavy alternatives. For players who want to finish rallies from the baseline with steep, heavy smashes, the Nitrix Thunder or Battle 600 are the right choices. The Typhoon's attacking shots are fast and flat — the speed-first identity means power is the deliberate trade-off for handling speed.
Technology Breakdown of Hundred Flareon Typhoon Badminton Racket:

The Typhoon's head-light balance concentrates mass toward the handle, reducing the rotational inertia of the frame head. The same Superlight Carbon as the Nitrix 10 and Flareon 100 — low mass for fast acceleration. Torsion Stop System — Accuracy at Speed:

Resists frame rotation on impact during fast exchanges. When the racket is used in rapid rally mode — the Typhoon's primary operating environment — contact is often slightly off-centre. Torsion Stop reduces the shot direction error from this off-centre impact, keeping drives and pushes going where they are intended even in the fastest exchanges.

Vibration-dampening foam within the frame absorbs residual impact energy without removing shuttle feedback. For a racket used in fast, high-frequency rally exchanges, CNTRL Foam reduces cumulative impact fatigue across a session — keeping the feel clean throughout extended doubles or mixed doubles matches.

Curve² enlarges the effective sweet spot across the string bed. In fast exchanges where perfect contact consistency is harder to maintain than in measured baseline play, Curve² geometry reduces the shot quality penalty for slightly off-centre contact — making the Typhoon's speed play more reliable across a fast rally.

The Hundred Flareon 100 is the entry point into Hundred's Flareon series — the speed-focused arm of their lineup, positioned as the Nanoflare equivalent by international retailers. The Flareon 100 delivers the basic Flareon identity at the series entry price: Superlight Carbon fibre, flexible shaft, speed-focused balance, and a 30 lbs tension ceiling that confirms its entry-level positioning.

The critical contextual note for players familiar with Yonex's Nanoflare series: the Flareon 100 is the entry-level Nanoflare-equivalent, not the fully expressed speed experience. Head-light balance is the defining characteristic of dedicated speed and defence rackets like the Nanoflare series. The Flareon 100's speed-focused balance is not head-light — it is somewhere between even and head-heavy, providing good swing speed without the extreme head-lightness of the Typhoon. For players who specifically want the head-light Nanoflare-equivalent speed experience, the Typhoon is the right choice.

For beginners and budget-conscious players who want a light, fast Flareon series racket with accessible entry price, the Flareon 100 does the job well. The Superlight Carbon keeps the total swing weight low for fast acceleration, the flexible shaft assists power for developing players, and the speed-focused balance makes the racket comfortable for doubles, mixed, and multi-format players. The 30 lbs ceiling is the main constraint at the beginner-to-intermediate level.

Head-heavy rackets (Nitrix 10, Predator 82/79, Flareon Typhoon, T-Fusion series) all trade handling recovery speed for smash momentum. The Hyfonic 1's even balance means no such trade-off — the racket is equally comfortable from the baseline, mid-court, and net, transitioning smoothly between offensive and defensive positions. This is the ideal specification for intermediate players who want to develop a complete all-court game rather than a single-dimension attack.

High-modulus graphite provides a meaningful quality advantage for a control racket — the higher stiffness-to-weight ratio produces clearer shuttle impact feedback, which helps players calibrate the touch needed for drop shots, net kills, and cross-court placements. For beginners developing their feel for different shot types, this clearer feedback accelerates skill development compared to softer, less responsive graphite alternatives.

The 30 lbs tension ceiling is shared with the Nitrix 10 and Flareon 100 — the lowest ceiling in the range. For control-oriented play where string tension directly affects placement precision and touch, this constraint is notable. Players who want to develop their control game at higher tensions (26–30 lbs) will find the 30 lbs ceiling limiting. The Hyfonic Lazer (32 lbs, also Hyfonic series) is the more appropriate choice if tension headroom matters.

In Hundred's three-series architecture, the Nitrix is attack (Astrox-equivalent), the Flareon is speed (Nanoflare-equivalent), and the Hyfonic is control (Arcsaber-equivalent). The Hyfonic 1's balanced feel, high-modulus graphite frame, and flexible shaft are all calibrated for players who want clinical shot placement and consistent rally precision rather than raw smash power or maximum swing speed.

The balanced (even) feel is the defining characteristic that separates the Hyfonic 1 from everything else in Hundred's accessible range at GOS. Head-heavy rackets (Nitrix 10, Predator 82/79, Flareon Typhoon, T-Fusion series) all trade handling recovery speed for smash momentum. The Hyfonic 1's even balance means no such trade-off — the racket is equally comfortable from the baseline, mid-court, and net, transitioning smoothly between offensive and defensive positions. This is the ideal specification for intermediate players who want to develop a complete all-court game rather than a single-dimension attack.

High-modulus graphite provides a meaningful quality advantage for a control racket — the higher stiffness-to-weight ratio produces clearer shuttle impact feedback, which helps players calibrate the touch needed for drop shots, net kills, and cross-court placements. For beginners developing their feel for different shot types, this clearer feedback accelerates skill development compared to softer, less responsive graphite alternatives.

The 30 lbs tension ceiling is shared with the Nitrix 10 and Flareon 100 — the lowest ceiling in the range. For control-oriented play where string tension directly affects placement precision and touch, this constraint is notable. Players who want to develop their control game at higher tensions (26–30 lbs) will find the 30 lbs ceiling limiting. The Hyfonic Lazer (32 lbs, also Hyfonic series) is the more appropriate choice if tension headroom matters.

High-modulus graphite has higher stiffness-to-weight ratio than standard graphite — stiffer and lighter per unit of material. For a control racket, this translates to clearer shuttle impact feedback on every shot, enabling more accurate shot calibration for drops, net work, and precise placements. The frame transmits contact information more faithfully than lower-modulus alternatives, helping control-oriented players develop consistent touch across shot types.

The Hyfonic series' defining characteristic — even mass distribution between head and handle. No directional bias means the racket handles well from all court positions, transitions easily between attacking and defensive shots, and maintains consistent playability in both net and baseline situations. The Arcsaber-equivalent balance philosophy in accessible racket form.

The flexible shaft provides elastic energy return on smashes while also assisting touch on controlled drops — the shaft's flex accommodates both power and finesse applications. For a control-oriented player who plays all shot types, the flexible shaft's versatility across power and precision applications suits the Hyfonic 1's all-court intent.

The Hyfonic 1 supports both playing profiles within the same control-oriented construction.
